outcome_evidence: In base_image, the robot separates the initially nested cups (frames 203–391), builds a small stack (frames 447–581), and then brings the cups together again (frames 685–906). The final placement fails: the last handled cup tilts during release and falls onto its side behind the remaining upright cup arrangement (frames 907–953). Thus packing is visibly unsuccessful, rather than merely unconfirmed; no completed final packed stack is shown.

failure_annotations.explanation: In base_image frame 907, the cup being placed by the image-left gripper begins tilting instead of seating securely over the other cups. As the gripper opens and withdraws (frames 912–929), the cup falls away; frames 940–953 show it lying on its side behind the upright arrangement. This unsuccessful final placement prevents completion of the packing task.
failure_annotations.recovery: Reacquire the fallen cup, restore its orientation, align it concentrically above the remaining cups, and lower it until securely nested before releasing; human intervention is not visibly necessary.
failure_annotations.severity_evidence: The cup falls onto the tabletop and remains accessible in base_image frames 940–953; no visible damage, spill, or meaningful damage risk is established.
failure_annotations.resetability_evidence: The fallen cup needs straightforward retrieval and reorientation on the clear tabletop; the robot could perform this reset without repair or substantial environmental intervention.
